haiku-low.q1: The 02:00 UTC trigger. It extracts replica orders whose updated_at is in the window: HWM minus 2 hours (excluded) to the cutoff (included).
haiku-low.q2: A bulk-import transaction can stay open up to 90 minutes after its updated_at, so its rows become visible late. Up to 90 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: The edit bumps updated_at, so a later nightly window covering that updated_at extracts it, and MERGE updates the existing dw.orders row.
haiku-low.q4: The delete is extracted as a write and merged with is_deleted = true. The row stays in dw.orders; rows are never removed.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt writes FAILED with the error, drops staging and exits. ROLLBACK first if inside the transaction. Retry after 15 minutes; after attempt 3, page on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show data through the previous committed night. At 06:00 UTC a staleness alert names the night and attempts, posted to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares the last 30 days of creation days and reloads any mismatched day from the replica by created_at.
haiku-low.q8: MERGE updates a row only when the staged updated_at is greater than the warehouse row's. Staging keeps one row per order_id, the greatest updated_at.
haiku-low.q9: In etl_state.orders_watermark. It is set to the window end, only if higher, inside the same transaction as the MERGE, visible at COMMIT.
haiku-low.q10: The merged rows, HWM and SUCCEEDED row commit in one warehouse transaction. Dashboards read only committed dw.orders, never staging.
haiku-low.q11: Staging is dropped when the attempt ends, so the failed attempt's staged data is discarded. The retry copies the same window from the previous attempt's run-log row.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads that creation day from the replica by created_at, with no updated_at window, in one transaction with the same MERGE guard. It never changes the HWM.

sonnet.q1: A scheduler trigger at 02:00 UTC (attempt 1). It extracts orders rows from the app's read replica whose updated_at is in the window: starting 2 hours before the HWM (excluded) up to the cutoff 02:00 UTC (included), in one snapshot. Deleted orders are included.
sonnet.q2: Bulk-import transactions can stay open up to 90 minutes after their updated_at, so the rows appear later than updated_at. That is why the window starts 2 hours before the HWM.
sonnet.q3: The edit raises updated_at, so a later nightly window picks it up. It is staged, deduped (greatest updated_at per order_id), and MERGEd into dw.orders, updating the row if s.updated_at > t.updated_at.
sonnet.q4: A delete is treated as a write, so the order is included in the extract. Staging sets is_deleted = deleted_at IS NOT NULL. The row is never removed from dw.orders. It stays with is_deleted = true.
sonnet.q5: The attempt writes FAILED with the error, rolls back if a transaction was open, drops staging and exits. If the process exits with no result, the scheduler marks the STARTED row FAILED and drops staging. After 15 minutes the next attempt starts, up to 3 attempts. If attempt 3 fails, on-call is paged and nothing reruns automatically. The HWM does not move.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show data through the previous committed night. At 06:00 UTC the staleness check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts naming the night and the attempts so far. It does not block dashboards or retries. On-call is paged only if attempt 3 fails.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares row count and checksum per creation day over the last 30 days, and reloads a mismatched day from the replica by created_at with the same merge rule.
sonnet.q8: Staging is deduped to one row per order_id, the one with the greatest updated_at. The MERGE updates a matched row only when s.updated_at > t.updated_at, so an older copy never overwrites a newer row. Running the same window twice changes nothing.
sonnet.q9: In etl_state.orders_watermark. The attempt process sets it to the window end (the cutoff), only if that is higher than the current value. It is set inside the commit transaction, in the same transaction as the MERGE and the SUCCEEDED row, just before COMMIT.
sonnet.q10: The merged rows, the HWM and the SUCCEEDED row are written in one warehouse transaction and become visible together at COMMIT. Dashboards read only committed dw.orders and never read staging. Any error before COMMIT rolls back.
sonnet.q11: The failed attempt's staging table is dropped when the attempt ends. The retry uses its own new staging table and extracts the same window, copied from the previous attempt's run-log row. It is not recomputed from the current HWM, so a retry at 02:30 still ends at the 02:00 cutoff.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads the replica rows for that creation day by created_at, with no updated_at window. They are applied in one transaction with the same merge rule, then compared again. It never changes the nightly HWM.
